segments.text: Every seven years, you get a brand new body. Well, that's not exactly true. Your body is replacing itself all the time, just at different speeds.
Your stomach lining is the fastest. It gets replaced every few days, because stomach acid keeps wearing it down.
Your outer skin renews itself every few weeks. In fact, a lot of the dust in your home is old skin.
Your red blood cells live about four months. Every second, your body makes millions of new ones.
Here's the wild part. Even your skeleton rebuilds itself. Bit by bit, you get a mostly new one about every ten years.
But some parts stay with you for life. Most of the neurons in your brain, and the center of the lenses in your eyes, are as old as you are.
So you don't get a new body every seven years. You're getting one every single day.
